feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 5 (score 580) is the best measured result. It cut yaw inertia (body 0.16 to 0.12 m, mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg) and moved the s-bend from 2 to 13 finishes, with line losses at 0.95 and oscillation at 0.298. The oval stayed at 20 of 20 with max_error 0.018 and oscillation 0.217, so the lighter, shorter body did not add jitter at that step. The slalom did not respond (0 finishes, progress 0.23, max_error at the 0.063 floor), which points to a separate limit on alternating bends. I kept the iteration 5 controller unchanged, so any change in this race can be attributed to inertia. Read the next race as follows. If the s-bend keeps improving (line losses at or below 0.95, progress above 0.858) and oscillation stays under about 0.35 on all tracks, the inertia lever is still working, so a further step (mass 0.5 with body 0.10) is worth trying. If oscillation rises above about 0.35 on the oval or s-bend, restore body_length to 0.12, since that keeps the mass benefit. If the s-bend plateaus near 0.86 progress with losses near 0.95 and the slalom still sits at its max_error floor, geometry has done most of what it can, and the next gain should come from a controller change rather than more geometry.
requested_changes: If the s-bend improves (line_loss_events below 0.95, progress above 0.858) and steering_oscillation stays under about 0.35 on the oval, s-bend and slalom, try mass 0.5 with body_length 0.10 to lower yaw inertia further, since iteration 5 showed the s-bend gain from the inertia cut and the mass floor is 0.4.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on the oval or s-bend at body_length 0.10, restore body_length to 0.12 and keep mass 0.6, since iteration 5 gave s-bend oscillation 0.298 and oval 0.217 at that body length.

If the s-bend plateaus near 0.86 progress with line losses still near 0.95 and the slalom stays at max_error 0.063, stop changing geometry and test controller gain (kd 0.6 or kp 2.5), since iteration 3 showed narrowing the track to 0.09 already raised s-bend progress (0.64 to 0.68) and iteration 5 showed the slalom ignores inertia.
